title.analysis: Authentic title "What changes After You Hit $100,000 In Savings" (lowercase "changes" as stored) is a milestone-curiosity frame. The script is about psychology and status at $100,000 of savings/investments, but it uses an 8% investment return throughout, so "savings" and "investments" are conflated; the promised changes are mostly asserted rather than evidenced.

script.opening_words: What if I told you that hitting $100,000 in savings doesn't just change your bank account balance, but actually triggers something financial experts call the 100,000 rule. What if I told you that this seemingly random number creates a psychological and mathematical shift so profound that wealthy people consider it the real starting line for building serious money. So, I most people think 100 grand is just another milestone on the way to becoming a millionaire, but they're completely missing
script.ending_words: constantly breaking down the financial psychology that separates people who build wealth from people who just dream about it. Drop a comment and let me know where you are on your journey to six figures. If you found this valuable, smash that like button to help other people discover why $100,000 is the most important milestone nobody talks about. Your future wealthy self will thank you for taking action today.
script.analysis: Full 21656 canonical characters read. A single-narrator psychology essay with no data sections: hook (the "100,000 rule"), $800 vs $8,000 at 8%, investment fearlessness, wealth identity, career confidence, social and dating dynamics, strategic spending, risk and time perspective, "financial telepathy", material desire, invisibility to predatory lenders, and an economy that depends on people not saving, then two consecutive closing summaries. Only the 8% arithmetic is concrete; most claims are asserted pseudo-research, sections repeat, and the stored text has heavy filler and ASR garbles.
beat_map: Two closing summaries and calls to action.

claim_audit.assessment: K02: 10,000 x 0.08 = 800; 100,000 x 0.08 = 8,000. Arithmetic correct, but the title says savings: the FDIC national savings average was 0.40% at the 9 October 2025 upload (FDICNR), so $100,000 in savings earns about $400, not $8,000. 8% is an average stock-market assumption, not a savings yield, and is not guaranteed each year.
